notes:
Deal overview: enterprise procurement for Dedicated capacity to support low-latency trading assistant and reranking pipelines. Heavy emphasis on guaranteed throughput and predictable reserved GPU planning. Legal + Ops are in parallel review for SLA and credits.

Key technical asks (from SE/infra):
- Sustained throughput target: support 8k-12k tokens/sec across peak microbursts; baseline traffic profile: 60% short chat requests (<=64 tokens) + 30% rerank batches + 10% long context (<=2k tokens).
- Latency SLOs: p95 <= 120ms for 128-token generation, p99 <= 300ms. Absolute hard cap for synchronous trading queries: 500ms.
- Reserved GPU planning: want capacity plan for initial pool of 8 GPUs (A100/80GB equiv) with autoscale headroom to 16 for scheduled events; clear pricing for standby reserved units vs burst.

SLA negotiation points discussed:
- Uptime target: Silverpine insists on 99.95% availability for Dedicated endpoints (proposes 4.38 hours annual downtime). Redwood initial standard: 99.9%. Ops pushback: need stronger credits for anything below 99.95%.
- Credit schedule: Silverpine wants linear credits: 10% monthly credit for 99.8-99.95, 25% for 99.5-99.8, 50% for <99.5. Redwood proposed tiered model with higher thresholds. Legal requested SLA language tying credits to monthly invoice for Dedicated capacity only (exclude incidental hosted bursts).
- Maintenance windows: Redwood proposed up to two 2-hour maintenance windows / month in non-peak hours (00:00-04:00 UTC). Silverpine counter: maintenance must avoid 13:30-21:00 ET (US market hours + pre/post). Suggested windows: 02:00-05:00 ET or Sunday 03:00-07:00 ET.
- Support response times: Silverpine requires P1 (system down impacting trading flows) response within 30 minutes and 2-hour escalation to engineering; P2 within 4 hours; 24/7 phone escalation for P1. Redwood's enterprise SLA aligns but legal asked for explicit SOC/benchmarked metrics.

- 2026-01-12: Intro demo (Jordan + Priya) — showed Dedicated throughput graphs and batching logic.
- 2026-01-29: Deep-dive with infra (Priya, Silverpine infra lead Matt Chen) — validated KV cache behavior, cold-start numbers. Fireflies: FF-98423.
- 2026-02-14: Pricing & TCO session (Jordan, Luis) — agreed on baseline RPU model, awaiting legal redlines. Drive: sla-draft-v3.pdf.
- 2026-02-28: Legal review kickoff (Silverpine GC + Redwood legal) — major topics: credits schedule, indemnity, data residency clauses.
- 2026-03-05: SLA negotiation call (Jordan + Priya + Silverpine CTO Elena Park) — CTO quote: "We need predictable uptime during market hours or the product is a non-starter. Credits must be meaningful."

POC / Milestones:
- POC run planned for week of 2026-03-21: 1-week dedicated pool (4 GPUs) to validate p95 latency under synthetic peak profile. Success criteria: p95 <140ms, throughput 6k tokens/sec sustained.
- Action item: Redwood to provide updated SLA draft with alternate credit schedule and explicit maintenance windows by 2026-03-15.

- Can assigned pool be pinned to specific HW (A100p vs A100S) in contract? SE noted thermal/driver parity concerns.
- How will autoscale billing for burst GPUs be invoiced vs reserved? Finance needs exact language.
- Are scheduled maintenance notifications guaranteed 7 days lead time + emergency maintenance <4 hrs notice with credit?
